rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods and Results <U+2014> two-year (2014<U+2013>2015) field experiment at the CER experimental farm near Bologna, Italy, in which a Cosmos probe was installed and its soil moisture compared with soil cores, profile probes and buried sensors (Table IV, Figures 7<U+2013>17).
rows.notes: The study validates Cosmos (CRNS) soil moisture against cores, profile probes and sensors (overall RMSE 0.0394), estimates effective sensing depth (within 0<U+2013>60 cm) and horizontal extent (at least 100 m), and computes a colour-coded soil moisture deficit (Figures 2b, 18) to indicate water stress. It does not test irrigation scheduling based on Cosmos, nor measure any water saving or water-use efficiency; the statement that Cosmos 'could be made operational for irrigation managers to determine when and how much to irrigate' is a recommendation, not a result. The study therefore supports only a precondition (accurate area-based root-zone soil moisture/SMD measurement) of the claimed optimisation of irrigation scheduling and enhanced water-use efficiency.

notes: Full text appears complete. Single-site study (one experimental farm, Po valley), two seasons; the reported RMSEs concern measurement agreement between Cosmos and reference methods, not any water-conservation outcome.
